newsitem.title: USA: Most airlines match American Airlines' fare cuts.
newsitem.headline: Most airlines match American Airlines' fare cuts.

text.p: Most U.S. airlines said Sunday they had reduced their ticket prices on selected routes, after AMR Corp.'s American Airlines slashed fares by up to 50 percent to woo customers scared off by a threatened pilots' strike.
Continental Airlines, United Airlines, Northwest Airlines Corp. and America West Holdings Corp. said they would offer competitive fares.
But both Delta Air Lines and USAir Group Inc. said they had not made a decision on ticket prices.
President Clinton intervened early on Saturday to halt a strike at the nation's second largest airline, appointing a board to study the dispute and postponing a pilots' walkout for at least 60 days.
Almost immediately after Clinton's intervention, American cut fares up to 50 percent on 21-day excursion fares, 40 percent on portions of tour packages and doubled frequent flier mile credits.
